children: Japanese rubber futures fell for a fourth straight session on Wednesday, weighed down by bond market-induced selloff in global equities that spilled into Asian markets, while the contract underwent profit-taking following its recent rally.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 3.6 yen, or 0.82%, at 433.5 yen ($2.70) per kg as of 0211 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 315 yuan, or 1.66%, to 18,645 yuan ($2,773.03) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) lost 70 yuan, or 0.46%, to 14,990 yuan per metric ton.

Japanese shares fell on Wednesday as renewed U.S. attacks on Iran pushed oil prices higher, stoking fears of an economic slowdown, while rising bond yields pressured growth stocks, with Japan's Nikkei
Following the recent price surge, the market has entered a period of profit-taking and position rebalancing, a Singapore-based trader said. The contract had hit a two-month high on Thursday.
The mid-term trend remains intact, with El Niño a lingering concern, the trader added.
Losses in rubber were limited, however, as oil prices extended gains amid escalating U.S.-Iran conflict.
Oil prices rose nearly 1% in early trade on Wednesday, as concerns over supply disruption intensified after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight.
Natural rubber often follows oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.

Elsewhere, Canada's border agency launched an anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigation on August 31 into exports of Chinese truck and bus tires, with a preliminary decision due within 90 days and potential provisional duties to follow, according to the Canada Border Services Agency's notice of initiation of investigations.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 231.8 U.S. cents per kg, down 0.9%.
